tasks.title: Ship immediate transcript readability fixes
tasks.description: Fix the most visible transcript issues without changing the underlying architecture yet. Wire existing tool label helpers into transcript rendering, replace `unknown` fallback with raw tool-name plus subtitle extraction, and keep reasoning collapsed by default so the page becomes readable immediately.
acceptanceCriteria: Tools that cannot be fully normalized display the best available raw tool name instead of a generic unknown label when a tool name exists
Transcript tool triggers use human-readable labels and args derived from existing parsing helpers instead of raw JSON-first headers
Fallback subtitles extract useful fields such as description, query, url, filePath, or path when available
Reasoning blocks remain collapsed by default and do not dominate the initial reading flow
Frontend tests cover unknown-tool fallback, human-readable tool trigger labels, and collapsed-by-default reasoning
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: This is the P0 slice. Prefer minimal changes that improve readability before introducing the registry refactor.

tasks.title: Create shared transcript tool parsing and registry foundation
tasks.description: Extract durable tool parsing helpers from the legacy card implementation and introduce a dedicated frontend ToolRegistry contract for transcript rendering. The registry should define icon, title, subtitle, badges, and content-renderer behavior for known tool families while preserving a generic fallback path.
acceptanceCriteria: Shared transcript tool utilities expose label, args, patch parsing, and file-change parsing without depending on legacy card-only components
A frontend ToolRegistry exists for transcript tool rendering and covers at least bash, read, grep, glob, webfetch, question, task, skill, apply_patch, edit, write, and fallback tools
Transcript components consume registry-provided title and subtitle behavior instead of hardcoded whitelist logic
Adding a new tool renderer requires a registry entry rather than editing multiple rendering switch statements
Frontend tests cover registry fallback behavior and at least one known tool-family renderer selection
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: This task creates the display abstraction used by later semantic rendering and live/replay convergence tasks.

tasks.title: Render semantic tool content and grouped context flow
tasks.description: Migrate transcript tool rendering to the registry so each tool family shows semantic content instead of raw JSON. This includes terminal-style bash output, markdown/file-oriented reads, file-change summaries for edit/write/apply_patch, animated running state, and stronger context grouping summaries for adjacent reads and searches.
acceptanceCriteria: Bash tools render command-first terminal-style content with readable status and output preview
Read and search tools render semantic content instead of JSON-first payloads
Edit, write, and apply_patch tools render file-change summaries as the primary view with expandable raw payloads
Adjacent context tools render as grouped summaries such as Gathering context with read/search counts and expand to individual tool details
Running tools use a distinct animated running state instead of a static pending dot
Frontend tests cover bash rendering, context grouping, file-change primary views, and running-state animation classes
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Keep grouping as a projection-layer concern. Do not remove raw input/output access for audit.

tasks.title: Improve reasoning placement within projected transcript turns
tasks.description: Teach the transcript projection layer to compensate for second-precision ordering by reattaching detached reasoning runs to the nearest following assistant block inside the same turn. The heuristic must be conservative: improve reading order without reordering across prompts, errors, or non-adjacent tool boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria: When reasoning parts and text parts share an ambiguous same-second ordering within one turn, the visible transcript no longer renders a detached thinking wall above the whole response
Reasoning reorder heuristics never move parts across prompt boundaries, error boundaries, or non-adjacent tool groups
Sessions with already-correct part order keep their original visible ordering
Projection tests cover same-second reasoning/text ambiguity, already-correct ordering, and boundary cases where no reorder should occur
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: This is the frontend-first answer to the thinking-order problem and should remain compatible with later timestamp precision improvements.

tasks.title: Align live transcript updates with replayed transcript semantics
tasks.description: Refactor live SSE transcript handling so it mutates the same logical tool and part shape used by historical replay. Shared normalization helpers should be reused for tool identity, file summaries, and merge correlation, with terminal events still reconciling through canonical detail refetch.
acceptanceCriteria: Live text and tool updates append into the same logical transcript shape used by replayed session detail
Live tool start/update events merge into one visible tool part when ids are present or inferable from normalized correlation keys
Terminal completion, failure, timeout, cancellation, and recovery updates trigger transcript reconciliation through detail invalidation or refetch
Representative live-then-refetch tests prove transcript grouping and tool identity remain equivalent after reconciliation
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: The backend transcript remains authoritative; live state is an incremental preview that must converge back to replay.

tasks.title: Add transcript affordances for diffs, copy, and metadata
tasks.description: Upgrade the transcript surface with the missing user affordances that make assistant output inspectable and reusable. This task adds richer diff inspection for file-changing tools, copy actions for assistant replies, and visible model/duration/session metadata in the transcript header or local footers without turning the page into a dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: File-changing transcript output exposes an expanded diff-oriented view instead of only a file list when before/after or patch data is available
Assistant replies provide a one-click copy action for the rendered response text
Session header or adjacent transcript metadata shows model, duration or running/finalizing state, and turn count without misleading terminal timestamps for active sessions
Transcript remains read-only and does not introduce a composer or control sidebar
Frontend tests cover copy action, visible metadata, and expanded diff inspection behavior
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Keep metadata embedded in the transcript experience instead of introducing separate control panels.

tasks.title: Implement follow-mode scrolling and streaming text pacing
tasks.description: Replace simple bottom snapping with explicit follow-mode behavior and add lightweight pacing for streaming assistant text. Transcript updates should auto-follow only while the reader is near the bottom, respect nested scrollable regions, and surface a clear jump-to-bottom affordance when new content arrives off-screen.
acceptanceCriteria: When the reader is near the bottom, live text and tool updates remain in follow mode and auto-scroll
When the reader scrolls away from the bottom, live updates no longer force-scroll and a jump-to-bottom affordance appears
Clicking jump-to-bottom restores follow mode and clears the new-content indicator
Nested scrollable regions such as code blocks or diff panes do not accidentally toggle transcript follow mode
Streaming assistant text uses visible pacing or typing behavior without changing the persisted transcript content
Frontend tests cover follow-mode pause/resume, new-content indicator behavior, and streaming text pacing hooks or rendering
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: This is the P3 interaction slice. Keep the model follow-mode based rather than event-by-event scroll forcing.

tasks.title: Increase session stream timestamp fidelity for new transcript events
tasks.description: Upgrade persisted session stream event timestamps from second precision to millisecond precision so new sessions preserve more faithful reasoning/text/tool interleaving. The migration must remain additive and backward-compatible, with legacy sessions still handled by the frontend reorder heuristics from earlier tasks.
acceptanceCriteria: Newly persisted session stream events capture millisecond-level createdAt precision
Historical session replay remains compatible with existing stored timestamps and does not require destructive migration
Transcript assembly or persistence tests verify same-second collisions no longer occur for newly written stream events under representative conditions
Tests pass: cd packages/cli && npm test
Typecheck passes
tasks.output: packages/cli/src/db/session-stream-log-repo.ts, related persistence tests or migration files
tasks.notes: This task is intentionally later because transcript readability should improve before storage precision work lands.

tasks.title: Add end-to-end regression fixtures and final verification
tasks.description: Add realistic transcript fixtures and final regression coverage across projection, live updates, and transcript UI so the change stays trustworthy after refactors. This task proves the transcript handles unknown tools, grouped context, reasoning placement, diff rendering, live/refetch convergence, copy/meta affordances, and follow-mode scrolling together.
acceptanceCriteria: Regression fixtures cover question/skill/task/webfetch fallbacks, read/search bursts, apply_patch payloads, edit/write file changes, and same-second reasoning/text ordering
Regression tests prove inferable tools do not render as meaningless unknown cards when a usable tool name or subtitle exists
Regression tests prove grouped context tools stay readable without hiding failures
Regression tests prove live append followed by refetch preserves equivalent transcript order, grouping, and tool identity
Regression tests prove copy, diff inspection, and follow-mode scrolling behavior
Tests pass: cd packages/cli && npm test
Build passes: cd packages/cli && npm run build
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Keep this task last so it can verify the integrated transcript experience instead of only one isolated layer.
